questions.problem:
Which of the following are affine transformations?

- ${T}_{1}:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}u+v \\ \sqrt{v}\end{aligned}]$
- ${T}_{2}:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}u+1 \\ {v}^{3}\end{aligned}]$
- ${T}_{3}:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}3u-2 \\ 8-v\end{aligned}]$
questions.worked_solution:
An affine transformation $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ is a function of the form

$$
x=Au+b,
$$

where $x,u,$ and $b$ are column vectors in ${R}^{2},$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

With this in mind, let's look at each transformation in turn.

- Transformation ${T}_{1}$ is not affine since it contains the term $\sqrt{v}.$

- Transformation ${T}_{2}$ is not affine since it contains the cubic term ${v}^{3}.$

- Transformation ${T}_{3}$ is affine. Notice that ${T}_{3}$ can be expressed as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3u-2 \\ 8-v\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3u \\ -v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 8\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 8\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "${T}_{3}$ only."

$$
x=4u+av-2,\,y=bu+cv-3
$$

is shown below. What is the value of $a+b+c?$

$$
[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4 & -1 \\ 9 & 5\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -3\end{aligned}]
$$

$$
x=Au+b,
$$

where $x,u,$ and $b$ are column vectors in ${R}^{2},$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

We can carry out the matrix operations using the matrix form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}4 & -1 \\ 9 & 5\end{aligned}]}}\cdot \overset{u}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}}+\overset{b}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -3\end{aligned}]}} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4u-v \\ 9u+5v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4u-v-2 \\ 9u+5v-3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding elements, we obtain

$$
x=4u+(-1)v-2,\,y=9u+5v-3
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
a+b+c=-1+9+5=13.
$$

\mathbf x = A \mathbf u + \mathbf b,
$$

where $\mathbf x, \mathbf u,$ and $\mathbf b$ are column vectors in $\mathbb R^2,$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

With this in mind, let's look at each transformation in turn.

- Transformation $\mathbf{T}_1$ is affine. Notice that $\mathbf{T}_1$ can be expressed as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}u+v \\ v-2u+1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}u+v \\ -2u+v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}.\end{aligned}
$$

- Transformation $\mathbf{T}_2$ is affine. Notice that $\mathbf{T}_2$ can be expressed as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}u-v \\ v-u\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}u-v \\ -u+v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}.\end{aligned}
$$

In fact, the transformation $\mathbf{T}_2$ is a linear transformation.

- Transformation $\mathbf{T}_3$ is not affine since it contains the quadratic term $v^2.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "$\mathbf{T}_1$ and $\mathbf{T}_2$ only."

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Parametric Representation of an Affine Transformation Given its Matrix Form
canonical_examples.problem:
The matrix form of the affine transformation

$$
x = 3u-v + \bbox[Gainsboro,2pt]{a}, \qquad y = u + \bbox[Gainsboro,2pt]{b}v + \bbox[Gainsboro,2pt]{c}
$$

is shown below. What is the value of $a+b+c?$

$$
[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]
$$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
An affine transformation $\mathbf T:\mathbb R^2\rightarrow\mathbb R^2$ is a function of the form

$$
\mathbf x = A \mathbf u + \mathbf b,
$$

where $\mathbf x, \mathbf u,$ and $\mathbf b$ are column vectors in $\mathbb R^2,$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

We can carry out the matrix operations using the matrix form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ 1 & -5\end{aligned}]}}\cdot \overset{u}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}}+\overset{b}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3u-v \\ u-5v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3u-v+1 \\ u-5v\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding elements, we obtain

$$
x = 3u - v + \bbox[Gainsboro,2pt]{1}, \qquad y = u + (\bbox[Gainsboro,2pt]{-5})v + \bbox[Gainsboro,2pt]{0} \, .
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
a+b+c = 1+(-5)+0 = -4.
$$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Matrix Representation of an Affine Transformation Given its Parametric Form
canonical_examples.problem:
The matrix form of the affine transformation

$$
x = 5u + v - 6, \qquad y = 2u + 4v
$$

is shown below. What is the value of $a+b+c?$

$$
[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]
$$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
An affine transformation $\mathbf T:\mathbb R^2\rightarrow\mathbb R^2$ is a function of the form

$$
\mathbf x = A \mathbf u + \mathbf b,
$$

where $\mathbf x, \mathbf u,$ and $\mathbf b$ are column vectors in $\mathbb R^2,$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

First, notice that we can express the given transformation as

$$
[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]
$$

Separating the constants and expressing the linear part as a product, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5u+v-6 \\ 2u+4v\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5u+v \\ 2u+4v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}5 & 1 \\ 2 & 4\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
a+b+c = 1+2+0 = 3.
$$
